summary: This program models a printer's job queue: four filenames are added to the back of a queue, then a loop repeatedly looks at the job at the front and removes it until nothing is left. It shows the queue's first-in, first-out order in action.

lines.text: The variable is declared as the Queue interface but built from a LinkedList, so the code can only use queue behaviour while LinkedList does the actual storing.
offer adds a job to the back of the line, which is why Report.pdf ends up printing first and Invoice.xls last.
The total is captured before any processing starts, because the queue's own size shrinks with every job removed and could no longer report the original count.
Checking for an empty queue before each pass is the safe way to drain it; peeking or polling blindly on an empty queue would give you back null.
peek reports the job at the front without taking it out, so the queue is unchanged and the same job is still there for the next line.
poll is the one that actually removes the front job, handing it back so it can be reported as printed.
